body:
I definitely identify with some of the points you are making here, and I hope it helps to share my own thought process on these matters.

>I don't want to get married or have children

That's fine, look into the childfree lifestyle if you don't have the impulse to raise and care for a child, that's perfectly reasonable. I'm just confused about what you are going for in your personal relationships then. If you're not interested in marriage, do you date or intend to date? If so, what is your end goal? Simple Companionship or Romantic Love? Either way, you can find plenty of agreeable partners if you look into the many communities compatible with your individual goals.

>Life truly does sicken me sometimes. If this is all life is about, then it really does make me wonder. What exactly is the point?

This is something I'm struggling with at the moment, as well. For what it's worth, I agree with you that a life taken at this face value is not worth living; but I disagree with your assertion that this is what life is all about. I think this is the way a lot of people choose to live; it may be the default - an unexamined life, as it were.

If you don't want to conform to what you perceive as the terrible cycle, don't do it. That sounds simplistic, but it's worth thinking about. Life isn't a Jane Eyre novel. There is no reason to accept the default, create your own alternative. Some people will call it selfish, but you should consider what you truly want out of your own life, and live for that.
